newsitem.title: USA: Louisiana may fill rainy day fund with oil money.
newsitem.headline: Louisiana may fill rainy day fund with oil money.

text.p: The Louisiana Revenue Estimating Conference said state revenues would exceed forecasts by $228 million, and urged the state to use part of the surplus to create a $50 million rainy day fund.

State officials had previously said they expected a surplus for the fiscal year that ends June 30, but only in the $170 million range. They said some of the unanticipated revenues were the result of higher oil and natural gas prices.

The severance tax on oil and gas is expected to generate $63 million more than the $345 million forecast in August. Royalties the state collects from oil and gas produced on state land and submerged land are expected to be $69 million higher than the $185 million previously forecast.
Lawmakers will allocate some of the surplus funds during a special legislative session that begins Feb 23.

"I'd like to take some of the surplus this year and put it into a stabilization fund," Senate President Randy Ewing proposed. He said that would enable the state to cover any unexpected deficit and improve its standing with bond rating agencies.

The Revenue Estimating Committee also raised its estimate for fiscal 1998 by $125 million. But unless the state continues a $110 million sales tax set to expire this year, it will still fall short of the money needed to offset anticiapted reductions in federal Medicaid funding, Commissionerof Administration Mark Drennen said.
